title: ctf.catalog/1
description: The control catalog file, the file backend of ControlCatalog. It is what lets ctf.coverage.module_source name a compliance.tf replacement with no registry token. The release catalog is embedded in the binary and also published per release for vendoring. Written as YAML; this schema describes the document, whatever the serialisation. Unknown fields are ignored, so an additive minor bump needs no change here; a schema other than ctf.catalog/1 is refused.

version.description: The catalog version, the value Catalog.Version() returns and the run-level ctf.catalogVersion property reports. It is compared between a vendored file and the embedded release to detect staleness, so it has to be well formed.

hosts.description: Framework id to the host label of its registry endpoint, which is what {host} in a module source is replaced with. pci_dss maps to pcidss, so pcidss.compliance.tf. A label is not a framework id, which is why this map exists.

defaultHost.description: The framework id whose host label is used when --remediation-host names none. It must be a key of hosts, which schemacheck enforces.

controls.description: Every control the catalog knows, keyed by id. ControlsFor(resourceType) answers from resourceTypes.

clausesByFramework.description: Framework ids are the control catalog ids (soc_2, pci_dss_v40), the same spelling manifests use; hosts maps each to its host label.

enforcement.description: Optional. The layer that owns this control, and why. A catalog without it loads as before; a reader shows the layer as not set.

notApplicable.description: Optional. Framework id to the reason this control has no applicable clause in that framework.

notApplicableClauses.description: Optional. Framework id to the clauses of that framework no control applies to, each mapped to its reason.

modules.description: Which compliance.tf module covers which resource types. ModuleFor(resourceType) answers from here, and each resource type appears in at most one entry so there is no tie-break. Uniqueness across entries, and every other rule that relates one part of this document to another, is beyond what JSON Schema can state, so schemacheck enforces those in Go.

source.description: The module source template. ModuleFor returns it unsubstituted; the renderer replaces a {host} placeholder with the host label of --remediation-host, else of defaultHost.

controls.description: The control ids this module enforces. Every id should also appear in controls[].

semver.description: The semver.org grammar, so a numeric identifier carries no leading zero and every version here orders under a conforming comparison.
